title: Infection of Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells with Mycobacteria and Intracellular Load Assessment
author: Barclay, Walburg, et al.

steps.title: Prepare 7H9 broth
steps.instruction: Weigh 4.7 g 7H9 powder, add to 1 L bottle, add 900 mL Milli‑Q water, 2 mL glycerol and 0.5 mL Tween‑80 (final 0.2 % glycerol, 0.05 % Tween‑80), invert to mix, autoclave, cool to 45 °C.

steps.title: Make ADC supplement
steps.instruction: Dissolve 50 g BSA, 20 g dextrose and 0.03 g catalase in 1 L Milli‑Q water, filter through 0.2 µm syringe filter (Corning).

steps.title: Assemble 7H9 medium
steps.instruction: Add 100 mL ADC supplement (10 % v/v) to the cooled 7H9 broth, store at 2‑8 °C and use within 2 months.

steps.title: Prepare 7H10 agar base
steps.instruction: Weigh 19 g 7H10 agar into 1 L bottle, add 900 mL Milli‑Q water and 5 mL glycerol (final 0.5 % glycerol), invert to mix, autoclave, cool to 45 °C.

steps.title: Add OADC supplement
steps.instruction: Bring Middlebrook OADC supplement (Thermo Fisher) to 18‑21 °C, then add 100 mL (10 % v/v) to the cooled 7H10 agar.

steps.title: Pour and set agar plates
steps.instruction: Dispense 35 mL agar into each sterile 10 × 10 cm square petri dish (≈28 dishes per litre), let set ≥12 h at 18‑21 °C, store plates at 2‑8 °C and use within 2 months.

steps.title: Prepare cBD epithelial medium
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of DMEM and BEpiCM‑b; add 5 mL 100× penicillin/streptomycin to each 500 mL (final 1×); add 12.5 mL 1 M HEPES (final 25 mM) and 5 mL 100× Glutamax (final 1×) to DMEM; combine 250 mL each of the two prepared solutions; add 5 mL BEpiCGS (final 1 %); aliquot 40 mL portions, store −20 °C (≤6 months) or 4 °C (≤4 weeks).

steps.title: Prepare soft trypsin solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 150 mg trypsin, 50 mg EDTA and 500 mg glucose in 500 mL PBS, adjust pH to 7.45, filter (0.2 µm), add 5 mL 100× penicillin/streptomycin, aliquot 40 mL, store at −20 °C (≤6 months).

steps.title: Prepare SBTI inhibitor solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 500 mg soybean trypsin inhibitor in 454.5 mL KSFM, add 5 mL 100× penicillin/streptomycin, filter (0.2 µm), aliquot 40 mL, store at −20 °C.

steps.title: Coat inserts
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL PureCol (3 mg/mL) and 100 µL 0.1 % BSA to 10 mL cold PBS; pipet 400 µL coating solution onto each 11.9 mm‑diameter, 0.4 µm‑pore insert; incubate 12‑16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Trypsinize PBEC
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL soft trypsin to each T75 flask of PBEC, incubate 5‑10 min at 37 °C, inspect detachment under microscope.

steps.title: Neutralize trypsin and collect cells
steps.instruction: Transfer trypsinized cells to 25 mL tubes containing 4 mL SBTI, rinse flasks with additional SBTI and add to tubes.

steps.title: Centrifuge cell suspension
steps.instruction: Spin at 230 × g for 7 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend and count cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 6 mL cBD medium, count with hemocytometer or automated counter (optionally mix 1:1 with trypan blue).

steps.title: Seed cells onto inserts
steps.instruction: Dilute to 80 000 cells/mL in cBD medium containing 1 nM EC 23; remove coating solution; add 500 µL cell suspension (40 000 cells) to each insert; add 1.5 mL cBD + 1 nM EC 23 to the well beneath.

steps.title: Grow to confluency
steps.instruction: Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; change medium three times per week (500 µL apical, 1.5 mL basal); cultures reach 100 % confluency in 5‑7 days (verify microscopically).

steps.title: Switch to air‑liquid interface
steps.instruction: Two days after confluency, remove all medium, add 1 mL cBD + 50 nM EC 23 to the basal compartment (no apical medium), avoid air bubbles under the insert.

steps.title: Maintain ALI cultures
steps.instruction: Culture ≥14 days at ALI, change basal medium three times per week, twice weekly add 200 µL warm PBS to apical side for 10 min at 37 °C, then aspirate to remove mucus/debris.

steps.title: Pre‑infection antibiotic‑free incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate ALI cultures in antibiotics‑free cBD medium containing 50 nM EC 23 for ≥48 h before infection.

steps.title: Disrupt barrier with PBS
steps.instruction: Remove basal cBD medium; add 1 mL warm (37 °C) calcium‑free PBS to basal compartment and 200 µL to apical side; incubate 30 min at 37 °C (collect washes if desired, store ≤‑20 °C).

steps.title: Prepare TrypLE/Y‑27632 solution
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm TrypLE Express with 10 µM Y‑27632 to 37 °C in a tube.

steps.title: Dissociate cells with TrypLE
steps.instruction: Remove PBS, add 200 µL warm TrypLE Express to apical side of each insert, incubate 10‑15 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Collect single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: For each insert, place a sterile 1.5 mL tube containing 800 µL PBS; pipet TrypLE up/down to break clumps, transfer to tube; rinse insert once with the same PBS, yielding 1 mL total volume.

steps.title: Aliquot for CFU and flow
steps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL of each suspension to a new tube for CFU plating; keep remaining 900 µL for flow cytometry.

steps.title: Prepare unstained control
steps.instruction: Collect 100 µL uninfected ALI‑PBEC, add 800 µL PBS, centrifuge 395 × g 10 min at 18‑21 °C, discard supernatant, add 400 µL 4 % PFA for 30‑60 min, wash with 1 mL PBS, centrifuge 395 × g 10 min, resuspend in 400 µL FACS buffer (0.1 % BSA in PBS).

steps.title: Prepare Live/Dead stain control
steps.instruction: Collect two 100 µL samples of uninfected cells; heat‑kill one (30 min at 56 °C or 10 min at 70 °C), combine with live sample, add 800 µL PBS.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial fluorescence control
steps.instruction: Take 200 µL from each bacterial culture into separate tubes, centrifuge 10 min at 805 × g, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Wash all samples
steps.instruction: Centrifuge every sample (including controls) 10 min at 395 × g, carefully discard supernatant (pellets may be loosely attached).

steps.title: Stain with Fixable Violet Live/Dead
steps.instruction: Dilute Violet Fixable Live/Dead 1:800 in PBS; resuspend each pellet (except unstained and bacterial controls) in 100 µL stain, incubate 30 min at 18‑21 °C in the dark, add 1 mL PBS, centrifuge 395 × g 10 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL 4 % PFA to each pellet, incubate 30‑60 min, wash with 1 mL PBS, centrifuge 395 × g 10 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend for acquisition
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 400 µL FACS buffer (0.1 % BSA in PBS).

steps.title: Load samples into flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Transfer each suspension to a FACS tube equipped with a filter cap to remove aggregates.

steps.title: Acquire and analyze data
steps.instruction: Run samples on a spectral flow cytometer (e.g., Cytek Aurora); apply gating: time gate → singlet gate → live‑cell gate (negative for Violet Live/Dead) → infected‑cell gate based on bacterial fluorescence. Use unstained and single‑stain controls for spectral unmixing and compensation.

description: Mycobacteria like M. tuberculosis (Mtb) and non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) like M. avium (Mav) pose a significant threat to global health. The incidence of mycobacterial lung diseases is expected to rise, and there is currently no vaccine that offers full protection. Studying lung epithelial responses to mycobacteria is important to understand early infection events and further improve vaccine development. This protocol describes the specific steps to initiate mycobacterial cultures from cryopreserved stocks and maintaining them over time. Then, we describe steps to establish cultures of primary human bronchial epithelial cells (PBEC) and differentiate those by culture at the air-liquid interface (ALI). These differentiated ALI-PBEC cultures contain the dominant cell types of the bronchial epithelium, and ciliary activity can be observed. Next, we detail how to perform infections on ALI-PBEC using mycobacteria, and how to eliminate extracellular bacteria. Finally, we provide instructions on determining the intracellular mycobacterial load in ALI-PBEC via flow cytometry, colony forming unit (CFU) assay and fluorescence microscopy. Combining these three techniques offers detailed insight into infection efficiency of mycobacteria in airway epithelial cells and may be transferrable to other lung region cultures (e.g. nasal, alveolar). Culture media and agar plates should be prepared as described below before starting this protocol.
